alignments.note: Adversative ἀλλά rendered by the ASV's *yea*.

Intensive αὐτοί → *we ourselves*; the finite verb supplies its own *have had*, so both words belong here. Head on *ourselves*, the word realizing the αὐτός lexeme rather than the subject pronoun (rule 17); a head on *we* remains defensible.
ἐν → *within*, discontinuous under rule 15. Two English words render ἐν ἑαυτοῖς, so rule 94 forbids joining the pair into one unit.
Reflexive ἑαυτοῖς → *ourselves*.
Article → *the* (rule 19).
ἀπόκριμα → *sentence*.
The ASV gives *death* no determiner, so the article has no *the* to anchor; rule 21/23 leaves it empty and keeps the case preposition on the noun.
Genitive noun rendered *of death*; the case preposition rides with the noun and rule 17 heads it on *death*.
Perfect ἐσχήκαμεν → *have had*; rule 9 heads on the lexical verb, not the auxiliary.
Purpose ἵνα → *that*, the word introducing the English clause (rule 40).
Ordinary negative μή → *not*; no negative indefinite follows, so rules 41 and 59 do not apply.
Participle of the periphrasis carries the lexical sense → *trust*.

Periphrastic ὦμεν πεποιθότες: the copula takes the supplied subject and modal *we should*, the participle keeping the lexical verb. Head on *should*, the modal the finite verb licenses; a head on *we* is the competing reading.
ἐπί → *in* (rule 36: the preposition governing the phrase takes the English preposition).
ἑαυτοῖς → *ourselves*.
ἀλλά → *but*.
ἐπί → *in*.
The ASV writes a bare *God* with no determiner, so the article realizes nothing (rules 21 and 23); the English *in* answers to the expressed ἐπί.
θεῷ → *God*.

Second attributive article before a participle with an expressed head noun (θεῷ): rule 31's own example τῷ θεῷ τῷ κτίσαντι → *God who created* leaves it empty and gives *who* to the participle. Rules 32 and 90 do not apply, a head noun being expressed.
Attributive participle rendered as a finite relative clause; the relativizer is its helper under rules 7 and 31, headed on the verb.
Article → *the* (rule 19).
Substantival adjective νεκρούς → *dead*; rule 58's closing clause leaves the determiner with the expressed article rather than with the adjective.

review_notes: Reviewed unchanged: every s### and t### id is partitioned exactly once, 23 source and 25 target tokens all placed, and no unit needed correction.
s007 and s018 are unrepresented under rules 21/23 because the ASV writes bare *death* and bare *God*; the case preposition *of* stays with θανάτου and *in* stays with the expressed ἐπί.

s020 follows rule 31's stated example (τῷ θεῷ τῷ κτίσαντι → *God who created*) rather than rules 32/90, since the article governs the expressed head noun θεῷ. Rule 90 disclaims in terms any unit where a head noun is expressed.
ἐν ἑαυτοῖς and ἐφ᾽ ἑαυτοῖς each render to two English words, so rule 94's precondition for a compound prepositional unit is not met and both split; the first is discontinuous under rule 15.
Two hedged heads: s002 (*ourselves* over *we*) and s013 (*should* over *we*). Both are genuine competing analyses under rule 16, not mere idiomaticity; every other unit is unhedged.
